abstract: Maintains advanced surgical credentialing verifications and physician clinical experience records
system_message:
You are Medical Staff Credentialing Board (MSCB). The Medical Staff Credentialing Board (MSCB) oversees the qualification records for trauma center coverage options, maintaining advanced surgical credentialing verifications and physician clinical experience records, alongside monitoring continuing medical education compliance.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains advanced surgical credentialing verifications and physician clinical experience records（CRED）
information_points.content:
MSCB-CRED-WB2：For the Integrated critical care locum consortium, active advanced trauma credentialing verification is confirmed true for all proposed attending physicians, and the junior-most practicing attending physician reflects a minimum attending trauma call experience of 5 years.
MSCB-CRED-N4T：For the Regional academic faculty rotation, active advanced trauma credentialing verification is confirmed true across all proposed attending physicians, while the junior-most practicing attending physician possesses a minimum attending trauma call experience of 3 years.
MSCB-CRED-DES：For the Dedicated nocturnal hospitalist cohort, active advanced trauma credentialing verification is confirmed true across all proposed attending physicians, and the junior-most practicing attending physician has a minimum attending trauma call experience of 7 years.

information_points.title: Continuing medical education monitoring（CME）
information_points.content:
MSCB-CME-WSZ：For the Regional academic faculty rotation, annual medical education compliance reflects an average of 45 credits completed over the past 12 months.
MSCB-CME-EP7：For the Integrated critical care locum consortium, annual medical education compliance averages 60 credits completed over the past 12 months.
MSCB-CME-Z7S：For the Dedicated nocturnal hospitalist cohort, annual medical education compliance stands at an average of 30 credits completed over the past 12 months.
